subject: general
question: The monthly incomes of two friends Manjit and Keshav are in the ratio 5 : 9 respectively and each of them saves ₹48,000 every month. If the ratio of their monthly expenditure is 1 : 3, then find the monthly income of Manjit (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Cross-Multiplication Method for identical savings of ₹48,000:

Ratio cross-product difference = (5 × 3) − (9 × 1) = 15 − 9 = 6 units.

Savings cross-product difference = (3 × 48000) − (1 × 48000) = 96000.

⇒ 6 units = 96000 ⇒ 1 unit = 16000.

⇒ Manjit's Income = 5 units = 5 × 16000 = 80000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹80,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

• 15 − 9 = 6 units 144k − 48k = 96,000 
• ⇒ 6 units = 96,000 ⇒ 1 unit = 16,000 Manjit's Income = 5 × 16,000 = ₹80,000 

**Given:**

Ratio of monthly incomes of Manjit and Keshav = 5 : 9

Ratio of their monthly expenditure = 1 : 3

Savings of each = ₹48,000

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

**Calculation:**

Let the monthly incomes of Manjit and Keshav be 5x and 9x respectively.

⇒ Expenditure of Manjit = 5x − 48000

⇒ Expenditure of Keshav = 9x − 48000

According to the given condition:

⇒ (5x − 48000) ÷ (9x − 48000) = 1 ÷ 3

Cross-multiplying the equation:

⇒ 3 × (5x − 48000) = 1 × (9x − 48000)

⇒ 15x − 144000 = 9x − 48000

⇒ 15x − 9x = 144000 − 48000

⇒ 6x = 96000

⇒ x = 16000

Now, calculating Manjit's monthly income:

⇒ Manjit's income = 5x = 5 × 16000 = 80000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹80,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income & Expenditure Relation

The foundational equation for all such problems is: Income = Expenditure + Savings. Changes in any one aspect proportionally affect the others.

Cross-Multiplication Shortcut

When initial quantities are increased or decreased to form a new ratio, equating the cross-product difference of the ratios to the cross-product difference of the changes quickly yields the value of one unit.

Alternative Gap Balancing

If the savings for both individuals are identical, you can also multiply the ratios by suitable constants to make the horizontal differences between corresponding terms equal, directly revealing the exact unit value without applying any variables.
